label: Copy-phase outputs (after DEL) and first ~3 original inputs
explanation: Dense positional feature (56% of steps). Fires on every copy-phase step after <DEL> (rate ~0.78, 58% of mass) and on the opening steps of the original sequence (t=0 always active, t=1 75%, t=2 48%), decaying through the middle of the original phase. Largely suppressed on the <DEL> step itself (16%) and mid/late original tokens (orig_idx 3-7, rate 10-30%), with a slight rebound on the last original tokens of long sequences. Largest activations occur at early copy steps (recall_idx 1-3), reproducing the first few original tokens; token identity has only weak influence (lift <=1.2x). Not token-specific.

issues: All the factual claims check out on dev. Copy-phase rate is 0.778 with 58.1% of the activation mass; the rate is 1.00 at t=0, 0.745 at t=1 and 0.479 at t=2; the <DEL> step fires 16.1% of the time; orig_idx 3-7 fire 10-30%, with a rise to 0.27 at orig_idx 8. The top activations peak at recall_idx 1-3. Test scores are precision 0.764, recall 0.889, F1 0.822, mass recall 0.930, matching the report.

Token dependence at t=1 is stronger than the overall 'lift at most 1.2x' suggests. The t=1 rate is 1.0 for in_tok g, i, 0 and 2 (and 0.93 for u) against about 0.63-0.67 for most other tokens. Adding a token-gated t=2 term ((t==2)&isin(prev_tok,[g,i,0,2])) to the t<=1 version only reaches test F1 0.824 against 0.822, so this does not change the verdict.

About 22% of copy-phase steps are inactive, and I found no systematic predictor for them. Rates by out_tok range from 0.59 (out_tok '0') to about 0.80. out_count, in_count, repeated adjacent tokens and recall_idx barely matter. L<=5 gives 0.81 against 0.76 for L>=8, and the last copy step (to_go==0) gives 0.71. These are mild modulations, not a counterexample class.
Activations missed in the middle of the original phase hold only 7% of the mass and look scattered. The in_first==0 subset at t>2 is 0.7% of the mass.
Minor overclaim: the label says 'first ~3 original inputs', but t=2 fires only 48% of the time. The explanation states this rate, so it is acceptable.
